newsitem.title: USA: ImClone, Immunex in cross-licensing deal.
newsitem.headline: ImClone, Immunex in cross-licensing deal.

text.p: ImClone Systems Inc and Immunex Corp said on Tuesday they cross-licensed certain technology relating to FLT3/FLK-2 ligand and its receptor.

FLT3/FLK-2 ligand is a growth factor that induces the proliferation and expansion of CD34 positive and hematopoietic stem cells, which are used in cell transplantation procedures. Hematopoiesis relates to the formation of blood.
FLT3/FLK-2 ligand may also be useful in expanding CD34-positive cells for gene therapy, the companies said.
Under the terms of the agreement, ImClone, which has patents on the FLT3/FLK-2 receptor, exclusively licensed the receptor to Immunex for use in the manufacture of the ligand.
In return, ImClone will receive an upfront payment and a royalty on the sales of Immunex and its sub-licensees of FLT3/FLK-2 ligand world wide.
Immunex granted ImClone a non-exclusive license in the United States and Canada to use its patented FLT3/FLK-2 ligand, manufactured by Immunex, for ex-vivo stem cell expansion.
The license may be expanded to include other countries at a later date, upon the approval of American Home Products Corp, which has a majority interest in Immunex.
ImClone has also been given the exclusive license to distribute the ligand with its own proprietary products for ex-vivo expansion.
Immunex will also supply FLT3/FLK-2 ligand to ImClone, which will have the non-exclusive right to distribute for ex-vivo uses.
Immunex has begun Phase I studies with FLT3/FLK-2 ligand for stem cell mobilization.
